source_text: τουργικὰ εἰς διακονίαν ἀποστελλόμενα, διὰ τοὺς μέλλοντας κληρονομεῖν σωτηρίας.» Ἄνωθεν δὲ τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου, γνωσθήσομαί σοι, φησὶ, καὶ λαλήσω σοι, δύο που, καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι, καὶ διὰ τούτου δηλῶν. Ἢ γὰρ ὅτι ἄνθρωπος ὢν ὁ Χριστὸς, τὰ ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπου λαλήσει φύσιν, καὶ οὐχὶ μόνοις ἐμμενεῖ τοῖς τῆς κενώσεως μέτροις, διά γε τὸ εἶναι Θεὸς καὶ ἐκ Θεοῦ κατὰ φύσιν. «Ἐγὼ γὰρ, ἔφασκε, καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἕν ἐσμεν,» καὶ, «Ὁ ἑωρακὼς ἐμὲ, ἑώρακε τὸν Πατέρα.» Ἢ ἐκεῖνό που τάχα· γινώσκεται γὰρ ἄνωθεν τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου καὶ τῶν Χερουβὶμ, τουτέστιν, ἐν ὑπεροχῇ καὶ δόξῃ τῇ ὑπὲρ ἄνθρωπον, καὶ παντὸς ἐπέκεινα γενητοῦ, ὧν τὸ ἀκρότατόν τε καὶ ὑπέρτατον τὰ Σεραφὶμ, εἰ καὶ γέγονε σάρξ. Ἐκ χρυσοῦ δὲ τὸ ἱλαστήριον, καὶ αὐτὰ τὰ Σεραφίμ. Ἡ μὲν γὰρ εὐκλεής τε καὶ περικαλλεστάτη φύσις, Θεός. Ἐν ὁμοιώσει δὲ τῇ πρὸς αὐτὸν κατὰ μέθεξιν, τὰ γενητά. Τοῖς δὲ ἐν κύκλῳ καὶ ἀγχοῦ γεγονόσιν αὐτοῦ, τὴν τῆς ἰδίας καὶ φυσικῆς φαιδρότητος ἐπιμερίζει μέθεξιν, ὡς φωτὸς ἐπί τι τῶν πέλας ἀντανακλωμένου, καὶ λαμπρότητι τῇ ἰδίᾳ τὸ προστυχὸν καταυγάζοντος. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔχει, καὶ ἀπεξεσμένος ἡμῖν εἰς τἀληθὲς, ὁ λόγος. {ΚΥΡ.} Μετὰ δὲ τὴν τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου κατασκευὴν, καὶ ἑτέρως ἡμῖν τὸ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον σκιαγραφεῖ, λέγων· «Καὶ ποιήσεις τράπεζαν χρυσοῦ καθαροῦ.» Δακτυλίους τε αὐτῇ προσερειρῆσθαι δεῖν ἐπιτάξας, καὶ χρυσοῦς ἐμβάλλεσθαι τοὺς ἀναφορέας, μέτρα τε αὐτῆς καὶ εὐτεχνίας τοὺς τρόπους, καθ' οὓς ἂν γένοιτο λαχοῦσα τὸ ἐκπρεπὲς εἰς εἶδος τὸ ἀνωτάτω σαφέστατα διειπὼν, «Καὶ ἐπιθήσεις, φησὶν, ἐπὶ τὴν τράπεζαν ἄρτους ἐνωπίους, ἐναντίον μου διὰ παντός.» Χρυσᾶ δὲ αὐτῆς τὰ σκεύη, τρυβλία τε καὶ θυίσκας, καὶ μὴν καὶ κυάθους, καὶ σπονδεῖα γενέσθαι προστέταχεν. Ἆρ' οὐκ ἐναργῶς ὁ ἄρτος ἡμῖν ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ κατεδείκνυτο, προκεισόμενος κατὰ καιροὺς ἐν ἁγίαις τραπέζαις ἐκκλησιῶν, καὶ ζωὴν διδοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα. {ΚΥΡ.} Τρυβλία τε καὶ θυίσκαι, κύαθοί τε καὶ σπονδεῖα, καὶ τὰ δι' ὧν τῆς ἁγίας τραπέζης ἡ μυστικὴ καὶ ἱερωτάτη πληροῦται χρεία, οὐ τῶν θείων κειμηλίων τύπος ἂν εἶεν. ὦ τᾶν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀλλὰ ταυτὶ μὲν ἐν τῇ Ἐξόδῳ. Τραπέζης δὲ πέρι καὶ μὴν καὶ προθέσεως ἄρτων, κεχρησμῴδηκεν ὁ νομοθέτης ἐν τῷ Λευιτικῷ· ἀνευρύνει δὲ ὥσπερ τὴν ἐντολὴν, τίνα τε τρόπον ἡ πρόθεσις ἔσται, διδάσκει σαφῶς, λέγων οὕτως· «Καὶ λήψεσθε σεμίδαλιν, καὶ ποιήσετε αὐτὴν δώδεκα ἄρτους. Δύο δεκάτων ἔσται ὁ ἄρτος ὁ εἷς. Καὶ ἐπιθήσετε αὐτοὺς δύο θέματα, καὶ ἓξ ἄρτους τὸ ἓν θέμα ἐπὶ τὴν τράπεζαν τὴν καθαρὰν ἔναντι Κυρίου. Καὶ ἐπιθήσετε ἐπὶ τὸ θέμα λίβανον καθαρὸν καὶ ἅλα, καὶ ἔσονται εἰς ἄρτους εἰς ἀνάμνησιν προκείμενα τῷ Κυρίῳ, τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων
pass_a_gloss: [Heb 1:14 cont.] (spirits) leitourgika ministering, apostellomena sent out eis diakonian for service, dia on account of those mellontas klēronomein about to inherit sōtērian salvation. Anōthen tou hilastēriou from above the mercy seat gnōsthēsomai soi I will be known to you, phēsi he says, kai lalēsō soi and I will speak to you; dēlōn showing, as I suppose (egōmai), two things through this too. Either (ē) that Christ, being man (anthrōpos ōn), will speak ta hyper anthrōpou physin things above man's nature, and will not remain (emmenei) only in tois tēs kenōseōs metrois the measures of the emptying, because of being God kai ek Theou kata physin and from God by nature. For 'I and the Father are one,' he said, and 'he who has seen me has seen the Father.' Or perhaps that: he is known (ginōsketai) above the mercy seat and the Cherubim, that is, en hyperochē in preeminence and doxē glory above man and beyond every genētou created thing, of which the topmost and highest are the Seraphim, ei kai gegone sarx even if he became flesh. The mercy seat of gold, and the Seraphim themselves. For the eukleēs glorious and perikallestatē most beautiful physis nature is God; en homoiōsei in likeness to him kata methexin by participation are created things. To those around and near him epimerizei he distributes methexin participation in his own and natural phaidrotētos brightness, as of light antanaklōmenou reflected onto something near and kataugazontos illuminating whatever it meets with its own lamprotēti brilliance. PALL.: Orthōs echei it holds rightly, and apexesmenos polished eis talēthes to the truth is the logos account. CYR.: After tēn kataskeuēn the construction of the mercy seat, heterōs otherwise skiagraphei he sketches in shadow to Christou mystērion the mystery of Christ, saying 'and you shall make trapezan a table of pure gold.' Having commanded daktylious rings to be fixed to it and golden anaphoreas carrying poles put in, and having set out most clearly metra its measures and eutechnias tropous the ways of good craftsmanship by which it would obtain to ekprepes eis eidos to anōtatō the highest excellence of form, 'and you shall set,' he says, 'on the table artous enōpious loaves of presence before me dia pantos continually.' He ordered its skeuē vessels to be golden, tryblia dishes and thyiskas incense cups, kyathous ladles and spondeia libation pitchers. Was not ho artos ho ex ouranou the bread from heaven enargōs plainly katedeiknyto shown, prokeisomenos to be set forth kata kairous at times on holy tables of churches kai zōēn didous tō kosmō and giving life to the world? PALL.: Kai mala indeed. CYR.: Dishes, incense cups, ladles, pitchers, and the things through which hē mystikē kai hierōtatē chreia the mystical and most sacred use of the holy table plēroutai is fulfilled — would they not be typos type tōn theiōn keimēliōn of the divine treasures (stored valuables), ō tan my good man? PALL.: Pany men oun certainly. CYR.: But these in Exodus. About the table and protheseōs artōn the setting forth of loaves kechrēsmōdēken ho nomothetēs the lawgiver has uttered oracles in Leviticus; aneurynei he broadens as it were tēn entolēn the command, and teaches clearly how hē prothesis the setting forth will be: 'and you shall take semidalin fine flour and make it twelve loaves; dyo dekatōn of two tenths shall be the one loaf; and you shall set them dyo themata two rows, six loaves the one row, on the pure table before the Lord; and you shall put on the row libanon katharon pure frankincense kai hala and salt, and they shall be for loaves eis anamnēsin for a memorial prokeimena set before the Lord; on the day of the Sabbaths [cont. §10]

Having commanded δακτυλίους rings to be fixed to it and golden ἀναφορέας carrying poles put in, and having set out most clearly μέτρα its measures and εὐτεχνίας τρόπους the ways of good craftsmanship by which it would obtain τὸ ἐκπρεπὲς εἰς εἶδος τὸ ἀνωτάτω the highest excellence of form, 'and you shall set,' he says, 'on the table ἄρτους ἐνωπίους loaves of presence before me διὰ παντός continually.' He ordered its σκεύη vessels to be golden, τρυβλία dishes and θυίσκας incense cups, κυάθους ladles and σπονδεῖα libation pitchers. PALL.: Πάνυ μὲν οὖν certainly. CYR.: But these in Exodus. pass_b_english: Cyril: …ministering, sent out to serve for the sake of those who are to inherit salvation’ (Hebrews 1:14). ‘From above the mercy seat I will make myself known to you,’ he says, ‘and I will speak with you’ (Exodus 25:22). Through this too, I think, he shows two things. The first is that Christ, though he is man, will speak things beyond human nature, and will not keep only within the limits of his self-emptying (Philippians 2:7), because by nature he is God and from God. For he said, ‘I and the Father are one’ (John 10:30), and, ‘He who has seen me has seen the Father’ (John 14:9). Or perhaps it is this: He is known above the mercy seat and the cherubim, that is, in a preeminence and glory beyond what is human and beyond every created thing, the highest and most exalted of which are the seraphim, even though he became flesh (John 1:14). The mercy seat was of gold, and so were the seraphim themselves (Exodus 25:17–18). For God is the glorious and most beautiful nature, while created things bear a likeness to him by participation. To those who stand around him and near him he imparts a share in his own natural radiance, as light, reflected onto something near it, lights up whatever it meets with its own brightness.
Palladius: That is right, and the argument has been finely worked out for us in keeping with the truth.

Cyril: After the making of the mercy seat, he sketches the mystery of Christ for us in yet another way, saying, ‘And you shall make a table of pure gold’ (Exodus 25:23). He commanded that rings be fixed to it and golden carrying poles be put through them, and he set out very clearly its measurements and the methods of fine workmanship by which it would attain the highest beauty of form (Exodus 25:24–28). ‘And you shall set on the table,’ he says, ‘the loaves of the presence, before me continually’ (Exodus 25:30). He also ordered that its vessels be made of gold: dishes and incense cups, and ladles too, and pitchers for drink offerings (Exodus 25:29). Was not the bread from heaven plainly being shown to us here, the bread that would be set out at the appointed times on the holy tables of the churches and that gives life to the world (John 6:33)?

Cyril: And the dishes and incense cups, the ladles and pitchers, and all the things by which the mystical and most sacred service of the holy table is carried out: would they not be a type of the sacred treasures, my friend?

Cyril: But these things are in Exodus. Concerning the table, and the setting out of the loaves as well, the lawgiver has spoken his oracles in Leviticus. There he widens the command, as it were, and teaches clearly how the loaves are to be set out, speaking thus (Leviticus 24:5–9): ‘And you shall take fine flour and make twelve loaves of it; each loaf shall contain two tenths. And you shall set them in two rows, six loaves to a row, on the pure table before the Lord. And you shall put pure frankincense and salt on the row, and they shall be for the loaves as a memorial, set before the Lord. On the Sabbath day…

choices.why: κειμήλια = treasured stored valuables; probably the church's liturgical vessels; rendered 'sacred treasures' without adding 'of the churches'.
ἀπεξεσμένος (polished, smoothed) rendered 'finely worked out'; the Greek is passive with ἡμῖν ('for us'), so no 'you' is supplied.
Leviticus 24:7 LXX 'εἰς ἄρτους' rendered 'for the loaves'.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-word in Hebrews 1:14 (λει|τουργικά) continued from §8; ends mid-quotation of Leviticus 24:8, continued in §10. Exodus 25:22 is paraphrased (LXX order: γνωσθήσομαί σοι ἐκεῖθεν καὶ λαλήσω σοι ἄνωθεν τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου). Cyril writes 'Seraphim' where Exodus has cherubim, following his §8 identification of the mercy-seat figures with the Seraphim of Isaiah 6; kept as written. 'Exodus 25:17–18' marks his reference to the gold mercy seat and gold figures; 'Exodus 25:24–28' marks his summary of rings, poles, measures and workmanship (LXX numbering matches English in Exodus 25). 'Philippians 2:7' is cited for κένωσις (self-emptying), a clear term allusion. The subject of σκιαγραφεῖ / ἐπιτάξας / προστέταχεν is the One giving the command to Moses and is capitalised; ὁ νομοθέτης ('the lawgiver') may mean God or Moses, so it and its pronouns are left lowercase. κειμήλια = treasured stored valuables; probably the church's liturgical vessels; rendered 'sacred treasures' without adding 'of the churches'. ἀπεξεσμένος (polished, smoothed) rendered 'finely worked out'; the Greek is passive with ἡμῖν ('for us'), so no 'you' is supplied. Leviticus 24:7 LXX 'εἰς ἄρτους' rendered 'for the loaves'.

changes: 'measures of His self-emptying' -> 'limits'; κατὰ φύσιν now governs both 'God and from God'
light simile: ἀντανακλωμένου rendered 'reflected onto' (was 'falling back on')
Palladius: kept the Greek passive with ἡμῖν ('has been finely worked out for us'); dropped supplied 'you'; note updated
Leviticus 24:5: 'shall be of two tenths' -> 'shall contain two tenths'
